sections.title: ESCRS 2026 Core Focus Areas
content: Next-generation artificial intelligence biometry formulas (Barrett Universal II, Kane, EVO 2.0, Pearl-DGS)
Light-Adjustable Lenses (LAL) and titratable postsurgical refractive technology
Lenticular extraction procedures (SMILE Pro, CLEAR, SmartSight, SILK) vs advanced LASIK
Combined Phaco-MIGS procedures in mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma
Corneal crosslinking (CXL) acceleration protocols (sub-epithelial and epi-on variants)
Presbyopia-correcting IOLs: EDOF vs Trifocal vs Extended Monofocal optical performance

sections.title: Corneal Ectasia & Biomechanical Instability
sections.content: Post-refractive ectasia arises from structural destabilization of the corneal stroma due to excessive ablation, thin percentage tissue altered (PTA > 40%), or unrecognized form fruste keratoconus. Tensile strength resides predominantly in the anterior 40% of the stroma. Lenticular extraction and PRK preserve deeper anterior lamellae compared to deep-flap LASIK. Intraoperative corneal elastography and Scheimpflug dynamic tomographic mapping (e.g., Corvis ST CBI/TBI) provide early detection before topographic changes occur.

references.citation: Ambrósio R Jr, et al. Integration of Scheimpflug Tomography and Biomechanics for Ectasia Risk Assessment. Cornea. 2023;42(5):541-552.
Santhiago MR, et al. Percentage of Tissue Altered and Post-LASIK Ectasia Risk. Ophthalmology. 2014;121(5):1001-1008.
Rampat R, et al. Comparative Optical Performance of Modern Presbyopia-Correcting Intraocular Lenses. Surv Ophthalmol. 2024;69(3):310-326.

sections.title: Advanced IOL Power Calculation Guidelines
content: For normal axial length (22.0 - 24.5 mm): Barrett Universal II, Kane, EVO 2.0, Pearl-DGS yield equivalent high accuracy (> 85% within +/- 0.50 D).
For long eyes (AL > 26.0 mm): Barrett Universal II with Wang-Koch AL adjustment, Kane, or Hill-RBF 3.0 to prevent hyperopic surprises.
For short eyes (AL < 22.0 mm): Hoffer QST, Kane, and Olsen (using C-constant) outperform traditional formulas.
Post-LASIK / PRK / RK: Use Barrett True-K, Haigis-L, or OCT-based formulas (RTVue) without relying on historical refraction data.
Total Corneal Astigmatism (TCA): Always measure posterior corneal astigmatism using swept-source OCT or Scheimpflug to avoid overcorrecting WTR or undercorrecting ATR astigmatism.

references.citation: Melles RB, et al. Accuracy of Modern Intraocular Lens Formulas in Standard and Extreme Eyes. Ophthalmology. 2018;125(2):169-178.

sections.title: Corneal Ectasia Screening Protocol
content: Step 1: Perform Placido Topography & Scheimpflug Tomography (Pentacam / MS-39)
Step 2: Evaluate Anterior & Posterior Elevation Maps relative to Best Fit Sphere (BFS)
Step 3: Analyze Belin/Ambrósio Enhanced Ectasia Display (BAD-D value; > 1.6 requires caution, > 3.0 indicates ectasia)
Step 4: Check Epithelial Thickness Mapping (Inferotemporal thinning surrounded by a ring of thickening indicates subclinical keratoconus)
Step 5: Measure Corneal Biomechanics with Dynamic Scheimpflug (Corvis ST CBI > 0.5 indicates biomechanical weakness)
Step 6: Formulate Plan: Proceed with LASIK, switch to Surface Ablation / SMILE, or recommend Corneal Crosslinking

references.citation: Ambrósio R Jr, et al. Corneal Tomography and Biomechanics for Modern Refractive Surgery Planning. J Refract Surg. 2022;38(9):590-602.

sections.title: Surgical Algorithm: High Myopia Correction
content: Step 1: Diagnostic Assessment: ACD > 2.8 mm (endothelium to anterior lens capsule), Endothelial Cell Density (ECD) > 2200 cells/mm2
Step 2: Myopia -0.50 to -8.00 D with adequate pachymetry (RSB > 300 um): Femto-LASIK or SMILE / SILK
Step 3: Myopia -8.00 to -18.00 D or thin cornea: Phakic IOL Implantation (EVO/EVO+ Visian ICL with central port)
Step 4: Intraoperative ICL Sizing: Use Swept-Source OCT sulcus-to-sulcus (STS) or ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) to target ideal vault (250-750 um)
Step 5: Postoperative Vault Audit: If Vault < 150 um (risk of cataract) or > 1000 um (risk of angle closure), plan lens rotation or exchange

references.citation: Packer M. Meta-analysis and Review of Outcomes of the EVO Visian ICL. BMC Ophthalmol. 2018;18(1):242.

sections.title: Femtosecond Laser vs Manual Phaco
content: Capsulotomy Precision: FLACS produces perfectly circular, predictable capsulotomies with higher mechanical resistance against tears if sized correctly.
Effective Lens Position (ELP): Reduced ELP variability compared to manual continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis (CCC).
Phacoemulsification Energy: FLACS reduces cumulative dissipated energy (CDE) by 30-50%, preserving corneal endothelial cell density.
Complication Profiles: FLACS carries a slight risk of intraoperative miosis (prostaglandin release) and capsule blockade syndrome; manual CCC remains faster and cost-effective.
Femto-MIGS Combination: FLACS creates precise clear corneal incisions and capsulotomy while simplifying simultaneous MIGS micro-stent placement.

references.citation: Day AC, et al. Femtosecond Laser-Assisted Cataract Surgery versus Standard Phacoemulsification: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Ophthalmology. 2016;123(7):1479-1490.

sections.title: ESCRS Endophthalmitis Guidelines
content: Intraoperative Prophylaxis: Intracameral Cefuroxime (1.0 mg in 0.1 mL) or Moxifloxacin (0.5 mg in 0.1 mL) reduces acute endophthalmitis risk by 5-fold.
Preoperative Prep: Povidone-iodine 5% in the conjunctival sac for at least 3 minutes prior to surgery is MANDATORY; topical antibiotic prophylaxis alone is insufficient.
Posterior Capsule Rupture (PCR): PCR increases endophthalmitis risk by 10-17x; ensure complete intracameral antibiotic administration and anterior vitrectomy.
Surgical Wound Integrity: Unsealed clear corneal incisions (CCI) invite tear-film influx; always check entry sites with fluorescein and hydrate or suture if leaking.
Acute Onset Red Flags: Sudden pain, severe visual drop, hypopyon, and dense vitritis within 1-7 days post-op require immediate tap-and-inject (vancomycin + ceftazidime) or vitrectomy.

references.citation: Barry P, et al. ESCRS Guidelines for Prevention and Treatment of Endophthalmitis Following Cataract Surgery. ESCRS Executive Committee. 2018;4(1):1-28.

sections.title: Surgical Red Flags in Refractive & Cataract Surgery
content: Preop Topography: Irregular astigmatism, inferior steepening, or asymmetric bow-tie on Placido disk (high ectasia risk).
Central Corneal Thickness < 470 um: Contraindication for LASIK; evaluate PRK or Phakic IOL after full workup.
Endothelial Cell Density < 1800 cells/mm2 in young patients or < 1500 cells/mm2 in elderly patients prior to anterior chamber procedures.
Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome (IFIS): Alpha-1 antagonists (Tamsulosin) cause iris billowing, prolapse, and progressive intraoperative miosis.
Post-Refractive IOL Selection: NEVER use standard diffractive multifocal IOLs in patients with prior LASIK/PRK due to severe loss of contrast sensitivity.

references.citation: Chang DF, Campbell JR. Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome Associated with Tamsulosin. J Cataract Refract Surg. 2005;31(4):664-673.

sections.title: High-Yield Clinical Pearls for ESCRS 2026
content: Presbyopia Correction: Matches optics to ocular surface quality. Mild-to-moderate dry eye patient? Choose EDOF or Extended Monofocal, avoid high-add trifocals.
Toric IOL Realignment: If a toric IOL is misaligned by 30 degrees, 100% of its cylinder correction power is lost. Re-align within 2-4 weeks post-op before capsular bag fibrosis.
Light-Adjustable Lens (LAL): Requires UV protection glasses until 2-3 lock-in sessions are completed; achieves uncorrected visual acuity of 20/20 in > 90% of eyes.
MIGS Integration: Hydrus Microstent and iStent Inject W combined with cataract surgery lower IOP by an additional 2-4 mmHg and reduce medication burden significantly.
Corneal Epithelial Remodeling: Epithelial thickening masks underlying stromal steepening; always utilize epithelial OCT maps in suspect eyes.

references.citation: Berdahl JP, et al. Toric Intraocular Lens Alignment and Astigmatism Reduction: Clinical Outcomes. Ophthalmology. 2023;130(4):412-421.

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Studies & Evidence
content: ESCRS Endophthalmitis Study: Intracameral cefuroxime demonstrated 5x reduction in post-cataract endophthalmitis rate (0.35% down to 0.07%).
SMILE vs Femto-LASIK 5-Year Data: Equivalent efficacy, safety, and predictability; SMILE showed significantly faster recovery of corneal sub-basal nerve plexus and tear film stability.
Pinhole Small-Aperture IOL (IC-8) Trial: Effective in presbyopia and highly aberrated post-refractive eyes by utilizing extended depth-of-focus small-aperture optics.
Accelerated Epithelium-Off CXL (Dresden 3 mW vs 9-30 mW Protocols): Equal efficacy in halting keratoconus progression while reducing procedure duration from 30 minutes to 4-10 minutes.
AI Biometry Ensemble Models: Integrating deep learning with ray-tracing formulas achieves > 90% of cataract eyes within +/- 0.50 D refractive target globally.
